subjective.vernacular: Over the past two weeks, have you felt down, hopeless, or lost interest in things you used to enjoy?
subjective.why_it_matters: Core DSM-5 criteria for major depressive disorder; presence of both depressed mood and anhedonia significantly raises probability.

subjective.vernacular: Do you feel tired or have very little energy most days, even after rest?
subjective.why_it_matters: Fatigue is a DSM-5 criterion for depression but also a cardinal feature of hypothyroidism, anemia, and PCOS-related hormonal imbalance.

subjective.vernacular: Are you sleeping too much, or having trouble falling or staying asleep?
subjective.why_it_matters: Insomnia and hypersomnia are both depression criteria; hypersomnia with fatigue also points toward hypothyroidism or sleep apnea.

subjective.vernacular: Has your appetite changed significantly — eating much more or much less than usual — or has your weight changed noticeably?
subjective.why_it_matters: Appetite change is a DSM-5 criterion for depression; combined with PCOS history, weight change also flags metabolic or endocrine contributors.

subjective.vernacular: Have others noticed you moving or speaking more slowly than usual, or have you felt unusually restless or agitated?
subjective.why_it_matters: Psychomotor retardation or agitation is an objective DSM-5 criterion that distinguishes moderate-to-severe depression from mild or subsyndromal presentations.

subjective.vernacular: Are you having trouble concentrating, making decisions, or remembering things?
subjective.why_it_matters: Cognitive difficulty is a DSM-5 criterion for depression and also occurs in hypothyroidism and anxiety disorders, helping differentiate causes.

subjective.vernacular: Have you had any thoughts of hurting yourself, not wanting to be alive, or suicide?
subjective.why_it_matters: Presence of suicidal ideation elevates severity class and urgency of intervention regardless of underlying diagnosis.

subjective.vernacular: Does fear of being judged or embarrassed in social situations stop you from doing things you need to do, like going to appointments?
subjective.why_it_matters: Documented social anxiety disorder is a known risk factor for comorbid depression and a barrier to care that must be addressed in any plan.
subjective.value: Social anxiety disorder documented; described as very hard to go to the doctor
subjective.missing: Current severity, treatment status, and whether anxiety is worsening alongside mood symptoms

subjective.vernacular: How long have you been feeling this way, and did anything happen around the time it started?
subjective.why_it_matters: Duration ≥2 weeks is required for MDD; identifying a triggering life event guides distinction between MDD and adjustment disorder.

subjective.vernacular: Are you currently having irregular periods, excess hair growth, acne, or other symptoms related to your polycystic ovary condition?
subjective.why_it_matters: Active PCOS is independently associated with depression and fatigue through hormonal dysregulation; symptom burden informs endocrine workup priority.
subjective.missing: Current symptom activity, menstrual pattern, and whether PCOS is being managed

subjective.vernacular: Do you drink alcohol regularly or use any other substances? If so, how much and how often?
subjective.why_it_matters: Alcohol and substance use are common contributors to depressed mood and fatigue and can complicate or mimic primary depression.

subjective.vernacular: Are you taking any prescription medications, over-the-counter medicines, or supplements regularly?
subjective.why_it_matters: Many medications (beta-blockers, corticosteroids, oral contraceptives, opioids) can cause or worsen low mood and fatigue; ibuprofen use noted but indication unknown.
subjective.missing: Dose, frequency, indication for ibuprofen; any other prescription or OTC medications

subjective.vernacular: Do you have trouble getting to appointments because of transportation, physical limitations, or other challenges?
subjective.why_it_matters: Documented mobility and transportation challenges increase risk of untreated depression and must inform care plan design (e.g., telehealth).
subjective.value: Mobility and transportation listed as challenges in shared care plan
subjective.missing: Specifics of mobility limitation and whether telehealth or home-based care has been considered

objective.vernacular: A 9-question validated depression screening questionnaire scored 0–27
A 7-question validated anxiety screening questionnaire scored 0–21
Blood test measuring thyroid gland activity — abnormal levels can cause depression-like symptoms and fatigue
Blood test checking for anemia and other blood abnormalities that cause fatigue
Blood test measuring iron stores — low ferritin causes fatigue even without frank anemia
Blood test for blood sugar control — uncontrolled blood sugar causes fatigue; last HbA1c 5.1% in 2019
objective.missing: Current fasting glucose or repeat HbA1c given 7-year gap and PCOS risk

objective.vernacular: Arm cuff pressure reading — a reading of 195/194 mmHg on 2026-07-03 is critically elevated
objective.missing: Repeat measurement to confirm; extremity comparison; symptoms of hypertensive urgency

objective.vernacular: Body weight relative to height — used to assess metabolic risk and PCOS status
objective.value: Weight 185 lbs (2026-06-14); height 220 cm (2021-01-11) gives BMI ~17.1 — likely data discrepancy
objective.missing: Verified height measurement; consistent BMI calculation; weight trend over time

objective.vernacular: Blood tests measuring male-type hormones that are often elevated in PCOS and linked to mood symptoms
Blood test for vitamin D — deficiency is common and associated with fatigue and low mood
Blood test measuring kidney function, electrolytes, and blood sugar — imbalances cause fatigue and mood changes
Clinician observation of appearance, mood, speech, thought process, and cognition during an encounter
Fingertip sensor measuring blood oxygen — low oxygen causes fatigue; rules out sleep apnea-related hypoxia as a screening proxy
objective.missing: Resting vs. exertional; no overnight oximetry if sleep apnea suspected

assessment_candidates.vernacular: Clinical depression — a brain condition causing persistent low mood, loss of interest, and other symptoms lasting at least two weeks
assessment_candidates.basis: Social anxiety disorder is a well-established risk factor for MDD; presenting complaint of low mood and fatigue is consistent; PHQ-9 required to confirm.
assessment_candidates.confidence_note: Cannot confirm without PHQ-9 and full symptom history; probability is a prior estimate based on presenting complaint and known anxiety disorder.
assessment_candidates.severity_vernacular: Untreated major depression causes prolonged suffering, impairs function, worsens physical health outcomes, and carries risk of self-harm.

assessment_candidates.term: Depression secondary to PCOS / hormonal dysregulation
assessment_candidates.vernacular: Low mood and fatigue caused or worsened by the hormonal imbalance that comes with polycystic ovary syndrome
assessment_candidates.basis: PCOS (E28.2, onset 2005) is independently associated with depression at 2–3× the population rate, mediated by androgen excess, insulin resistance, and hypothalamic-pituitary-ovarian axis disruption.
assessment_candidates.confidence_note: PCOS is documented but current activity unknown; hormonal labs have not been drawn; this is biologically plausible and clinically important to distinguish from primary MDD.
assessment_candidates.severity_vernacular: If untreated hormonal dysregulation is driving mood symptoms, antidepressants alone will give incomplete relief; the underlying PCOS must also be managed.

assessment_candidates.vernacular: An underactive thyroid gland that slows the body's metabolism, causing fatigue, low mood, weight gain, and cognitive slowing
assessment_candidates.basis: Hypothyroidism is common in women of reproductive age, is associated with PCOS, and presents identically to depression; TSH is mandatory in any fatigue/low mood workup.
assessment_candidates.confidence_note: No thyroid labs available; cannot rule in or out without TSH.
assessment_candidates.severity_vernacular: Untreated hypothyroidism worsens over time and, if missed, means the patient receives antidepressants instead of thyroid replacement — a correctable but prolonged error.

assessment_candidates.vernacular: Low iron stores — with or without full anemia — that cause fatigue, poor concentration, and low mood
assessment_candidates.basis: Iron deficiency is common in premenopausal women, causes fatigue and mood symptoms, and is correctable; PCOS with irregular periods may alter menstrual blood loss patterns.
assessment_candidates.confidence_note: No CBC or ferritin available; cannot assess without these labs.
assessment_candidates.severity_vernacular: Untreated iron deficiency causes ongoing fatigue and cognitive impairment; treatable with supplementation once identified.

assessment_candidates.vernacular: A stress reaction where significant life stressors (not a biological illness) cause low mood that does not fully meet criteria for major depression
assessment_candidates.basis: Documented social anxiety, mobility challenges, and transportation barriers represent chronic psychosocial stressors that can precipitate adjustment disorder; distinguishable from MDD by PHQ-9 score and onset history.
assessment_candidates.confidence_note: Cannot distinguish from MDD without symptom duration, severity, and trigger history.
assessment_candidates.severity_vernacular: If unrecognized, stress-related mood symptoms persist and can progress to full MDD; psychosocial support is effective when identified early.

assessment_candidates.vernacular: Low levels of vitamin D, which is linked to fatigue and low mood, especially with limited sun exposure or mobility
not_yet_testable: o-010 (vitamin D level — not yet ordered)
assessment_candidates.basis: Vitamin D deficiency is prevalent in people with limited mobility and outdoor activity; associated with fatigue and depressive symptoms in multiple observational studies.
assessment_candidates.confidence_note: No vitamin D level available; this is a modifiable and commonly overlooked contributor.
assessment_candidates.severity_vernacular: Deficiency is easily corrected with supplementation; if missed, contributes to ongoing fatigue and mood symptoms.

assessment_candidates.term: Hypertensive crisis / hypertension-related mood and fatigue
assessment_candidates.vernacular: Extremely high blood pressure (195/194 mmHg recorded) causing or contributing to physical symptoms including headache, fatigue, and poor wellbeing
not_yet_testable: o-011 (BMP for end-organ assessment — not yet ordered)
assessment_candidates.basis: Blood pressure of 195/194 mmHg recorded 2026-07-03 constitutes hypertensive urgency (or emergency if symptoms present); severe hypertension independently causes fatigue, headache, and mood dysregulation, and is itself a life-threatening finding requiring urgent reassessment.
assessment_candidates.confidence_note: Single reading may reflect measurement error (prior reading 120/60 one month earlier); urgent repeat measurement is required before this can be confirmed or dismissed.
assessment_candidates.severity_vernacular: Unaddressed hypertensive urgency/emergency can cause stroke, heart attack, or kidney failure — this finding requires same-day clarification regardless of the depression workup.

residual.vernacular: Something not on this list — the differential is never closed

plan_options.term: Urgent blood pressure re-measurement and hypertensive urgency evaluation
plan_options.vernacular: Repeat the blood pressure reading today using correct technique; if confirmed ≥180/120 mmHg, assess for symptoms of end-organ damage (headache, vision changes, chest pain) and arrange same-day emergency care
plan_options.basis: JNC 8 and AHA/ACC guidelines define BP ≥180/120 as hypertensive urgency requiring same-day evaluation; prior reading of 195/194 mmHg cannot be dismissed without confirmation.
plan_options.who_can_act: Primary care provider, nurse, or emergency clinician

plan_options.vernacular: Complete the standard 9-question depression screening tool to score symptom severity and guide next steps
plan_options.basis: PHQ-9 is validated, guideline-recommended (USPSTF Grade B) for depression screening and severity staging; required before diagnosis can be confirmed.
plan_options.who_can_act: Patient (self-administered), clinician, or care coordinator; telehealth-compatible

plan_options.vernacular: Complete the standard 7-question anxiety screening tool to quantify current anxiety severity alongside mood symptoms
plan_options.basis: GAD-7 is validated for anxiety screening and is complementary to PHQ-9 given documented social anxiety disorder; identifies comorbid anxiety that modifies treatment approach.
plan_options.who_can_act: Patient (self-administered), clinician, or care coordinator; telehealth-compatible

plan_options.vernacular: Blood test to check whether the thyroid gland is working normally — an underactive thyroid mimics depression
plan_options.basis: USPSTF and endocrine society guidelines recommend TSH as first-line in evaluation of fatigue and mood symptoms; especially indicated with PCOS comorbidity.
plan_options.who_can_act: Primary care provider or endocrinologist to order; phlebotomy or in-home blood draw

plan_options.term: CBC with differential and serum ferritin
plan_options.vernacular: Blood tests to check for anemia and iron stores — low iron is a treatable cause of fatigue
plan_options.basis: Standard first-line labs in fatigue workup; ferritin is more sensitive than hemoglobin alone for iron deficiency.
plan_options.who_can_act: Primary care provider to order; phlebotomy or in-home blood draw

plan_options.term: PCOS hormonal panel (testosterone, DHEA-S, LH/FSH, prolactin)
plan_options.vernacular: Blood tests to check whether PCOS-related hormones are out of balance and contributing to mood symptoms
plan_options.basis: Endocrine Society PCOS guidelines recommend periodic reassessment of androgen levels; relevant to mood and metabolic risk stratification.
plan_options.who_can_act: Primary care provider or gynecologist/endocrinologist to order

plan_options.vernacular: Blood test to check vitamin D — deficiency is common with limited mobility and linked to fatigue and low mood
plan_options.basis: Vitamin D deficiency is highly prevalent and correctable; recommended in fatigue workup particularly with mobility limitations.

plan_options.term: Telehealth or home-visit referral to behavioral health
plan_options.vernacular: Connect with a mental health provider through video call or home visit to reduce barriers caused by social anxiety, mobility, and transportation
plan_options.basis: Telehealth for depression is non-inferior to in-person care (APA, SAMHSA evidence base); essential given documented social anxiety disorder and access barriers.
plan_options.who_can_act: Primary care provider to refer; care coordinator to arrange; patient to consent

plan_options.vernacular: Ask directly and document whether the patient has any thoughts of self-harm or suicide — this is always required when depression is possible
plan_options.basis: Standard of care in any depression evaluation; Columbia Suicide Severity Rating Scale (C-SSRS) is validated and can be administered remotely.
plan_options.who_can_act: Primary care provider, mental health clinician, or trained care coordinator
